props.title: Spot the Fake — Part 1
props.sub: The finfluencer machine SEBI is dismantling

props.name: Avadhut Sathe
props.charge: Collected ~Rs 601 cr from over 3.37 lakh people under the cover of 'education' — SEBI called it unregistered advisory built on selective profit-showcasing, and ordered Rs 546.16 cr disgorged.
props.lesson: "Education" that shows you only the winning trades is not education.

props.name: Asmita Patel
props.alias: The She-Wolf of the stock market
props.charge: Marketed 'courses' that were really unregistered buy/sell advisory; of ~Rs 104 cr earned, SEBI impounded Rs 53.67 cr and barred her and five entities.
props.lesson: A glamorous nickname is a marketing budget, not a track record.

props.name: Md Nasiruddin Ansari
props.charge: Built a massive following as a chart 'guru', then sold unregistered advisory; SEBI barred him and ordered Rs 17.2 cr disgorged.
props.lesson: A catchy handle and a big following prove reach — never returns.

captions: Chapter thirteen. Now the other half of the story
— the fakes.

Because while real investors were quietly
compounding, an entire

industry was manufacturing fake success. And the
regulator has
receipts.
Start with the biggest.

In December twenty twenty-five, SEBI came down on
Avadhut
Sathe and his trading academy.

Over eight years, they had collected around six
hundred
and one crore rupees from more than three lakh
people — under the banner of 'education'.

SEBI found it was really unregistered investment
advice, built
on showing off selective wins — and ordered five
hundred and forty-six crore disgorged.
Read that number again. That is the size of
the fake-success industry.

Then there's Asmita Patel, who branded herself the
she-wolf
of the stock market and the options queen.
SEBI barred her in February twenty twenty-five.

Her 'courses', the regulator said, were really
unregistered buy-and-sell
advice — and of roughly one hundred and four

crore rupees earned, more than fifty-three crore was
impounded.
The glamorous nickname wasn't a track record. It was
a marketing budget.
And the one that named the whole genre —
'Baap of Chart', the self-styled father of charts.

A huge following, a confident persona, and, SEBI
found,

unregistered advisory underneath — with seventeen
crore rupees ordered
disgorged back in twenty twenty-three.
Three names, one template.

Build an audience, promise the dream, sell the
course.

The trading profits were never the business. You
were.
